title: Cap. III Rej. Rat. 1: Augustine Ep. 107 / 1 Tim. 2:4 — God not willing all alike
pass_a_gloss: And in Epistle 107, among twelve sentences which he affirms pertain to right and catholic faith, this is the fourth: We know that grace is not given to all men, and to those to whom it is given, it is given not only not according to the merits of works, but not even according to the merits of the will of those to whom it is given: which appears most of all in little ones. And not much later, regarding this very objection which is customarily urged about a common and indifferent will as to the salvation of all, he adds these words, most worthy of our recital and your observation: It is manifest that those who resist this so clear truth do not understand at all in what manner of speaking it was said that God wills all men to be saved, when so many are not saved. Not because they [will not], but because God does not will: which is manifested without any darkness in little ones. What therefore was said, GOD WILLS ALL MEN TO BE SAVED, when he does not will so many to be saved, was said for this reason, because all who are saved are not saved unless he himself wills; and if any things can be understood in another way, yet they cannot be contrary to this most open truth, in which you see that so many, with men willing, but God not willing, are not saved. Thus far Augustine.
pass_b_english: Epistle 107's fourth of twelve catholic sentences: we know grace is not given to all; and where it is given, not by works' merits, nor even by the will's merits of those who get it — clearest in infants. Soon after, on the usual "common indifferent will to save all" objection, he adds words worth quoting: those who fight this plain truth miss how "God wills all to be saved" is said when so many are not. Not because they refuse, but because God does not will — obvious in infants. So "GOD WILLS ALL MEN TO BE SAVED," though he does not will so many saved, means all who are saved are saved only if he wills; any other reading must not contradict that open truth: many are not saved though men will it, if God does not. So Augustine.
source_text: Et Epist. 107. inter duodecim sententias quae ad fidem rectam & catholicam pertinere affirmat, haec quarta est, Scimus gratiam non omnibus hominibus dari, & quibus datur, non solum secundum merita operum non dari, sed nec secundum merita voluntatis eorum quibus datur: quod maxime apparet in parvulis. Et non multo post, hanc ipsam objectionem respiciens, quae obtendi solet de voluntate communi & indifferenti quoad salutem omnium, haec verba adjungit, recitatione nostra & observatione vestra dignissima: Manifestum est eos qui huic resistunt tam perspicuae veritati, non intelligere omnino qua locutione sit dictum, quod omnes homines vult Deus salvos fieri, cum tam multi salvi non fiant. Non quia ipsi, sed quia Deus non vult: quod sine ulla caligine manifestatur in parvulis. Quod igitur dictum est, OMNES HOMINES VULT DEUS SALVOS FIERI, cum tam multos nolit salvos fieri, ideo dictum est, quia omnes qui salvi fiunt, nisi ipse velit non fiunt; & si quae alio modo intelligi possunt, ut tamen huic apertissimae veritati, in qua vides tam multos, volentibus hominibus, sed Deo nolente, salvos non fieri, contraria esse non possunt. Hactenus Augustinus.
